## 1.1.0

Replace the jar and restart. Your config is kept as it is.

### Added

- A developer API, like CoreProtect's, so other plugins can work with xRewind: they can log the blocks and items they change (so a plot reset shows in lookups and can be undone), look up the history, preview, apply and undo rollbacks and restores, and hold the writer for a moment while a backup copies the database. Plugins' lookups and rollbacks run like yours: in the background, a few milliseconds per tick, one rollback at a time. See [Developer API](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xrewind/developer-api/). It costs nothing unless a plugin uses it.
- Plugins can listen for rollbacks (and stop one before it starts), and for lookups, to keep an audit log of who looked up what, staff commands included. A staff member whose rollback, apply or undo another plugin stopped is told so.
- A purge or a CoreProtect import that the server stops partway says so, with how many changes the purge deleted by then.

### Fixed

- Clicking **Next page** below a lookup's results shows the next page. It ran `<next>` instead, which isn't a command.
- After a purge, the space is handed back to the disk a few thousand pages at a time, so logging never waits on all of it at once.
- A CoreProtect import can't wait forever for its last rows when one of them is a change the database won't take.
- `/xrewind reload` works on an empty server. Paper pauses a server that's been empty for a minute, and the reload waited for the next player to join.
- A rollback or restore typed in the console of an empty server runs straight away, not when the next player joins.
- On MySQL, a connection whose database stops answering gives up after five minutes, or ten seconds to connect, instead of holding the writer forever.

## 1.0.2

Replace the jar and restart. Your config is kept as it is.

### Fixed

- A rollback marks as rolled back only the changes it really made. Before, changes it skipped (a block this Minecraft can't read, a world that isn't loaded, or the rest of a rollback that stopped partway) were marked too, so no later rollback could reach them.
- A database that can't be reconnected to no longer leaks a connection on every try, which on MySQL could use up its connections.
- Three write failures hours apart no longer count as "three in a row": only failures back to back make xRewind write a batch row by row.
- `/xrewind page` goes up to page 500. Much deeper pages read thousands of rows to show seven.
- On MySQL, starting again after a database update that stopped partway carries on, instead of failing on the tables already made.
- A huge TNT chain no longer slows down as xRewind tidies its list of recent breaks, and a preview a player left without applying is let go of.

## 1.0.1

Replace the jar and restart. Your config is kept as it is.

### Fixed

- A rollback that takes under a second says how long to the hundredth: "in 0.04s", not "in 0.0s", which read as if nothing happened.
- `/execute as <player> run xrewind ...`, and command blocks running as a player, now measure `r:` from that player and can `#preview` to them. Before, they were treated as the console.

## 1.0.0

The first release. Drop the jar in and start the server: it logs to SQLite in its own folder, with nothing to set up. Coming from CoreProtect? Run `/xr import coreprotect` to bring your history.

### Logging

- Blocks placed and broken, with what they held (a chest's items, a sign's text), and the torches, signs and rails that fall off with them.
- Explosions (TNT is put down to whoever lit it), fire, buckets and liquids that destroy something, pistons, and mobs that change blocks (endermen, withers, falling sand).
- Items put in and taken out of containers, kills, sign text, and joins and quits.
- Off unless you turn them on: hopper transfers, door and lever clicks, leaf decay, chat and commands.
- Each kind is a switch under `log`, and one that's off isn't even listened for. `excluded-worlds` leaves worlds out.
- Logging costs about 40 nanoseconds per change on the game's threads: everything else happens on one background thread, in batches.

### Looking up

- `/xr inspect`: click a block to see its history, or place one to see what was there.
- `/xr lookup` with CoreProtect's parameters: `u:` `t:` `r:` `a:` `i:` `e:` `w:` and `#count`. `/xr page` and `/xr near`.

### Rolling back

- `/xr rollback` and `/xr restore` with the same parameters, `#preview` to see the result first, and `/xr undo`.
- Blocks come back with what they held, and items taken from containers are put back.
- Blocks are set a few milliseconds per tick, chunk by chunk (region by region on Folia), so even a big rollback doesn't freeze the server.
- A rollback needs `t:`, covers 10 blocks around you without `r:`, and past 100 blocks needs `xrewind.rollback.global`.

### Keeping it tidy

- Automatic purges, free: history older than 30 days is deleted once a day (`purge.keep-days`; 0 keeps everything), and `/xr purge`.
- SQLite by default, MySQL or MariaDB for networks. No driver is bundled: Paper and Folia include them.
- `/xr import coreprotect` reads CoreProtect's database (SQLite or MySQL) and imports blocks, kills, containers, sessions, signs, chat and commands.
- `/xr status` shows where the history goes and whether logging is keeping up.
